text:
Package 17 is a derivation program, not a closure claim.

The central open problem, in the author’s words, is no longer whether the retained-memory backbone is mathematically interesting. It is whether the full bridge operator and lattice framework can be derived from a microscopic law, shown to admit a GR limit, and shown to recover a viable cosmological pipeline.

A 3–5 Apr 2026 quadratic RG sprint (σ*≈0.7333, D_f≈2.7333, γ≈0.2667) is a prior scaffold on that cosmology seam. It named a remaining microscopic-amplitude gap and recorded a DESI-null frozen operator. Package 17, posted a month later, is still the derivation program. That sprint did not close it. The 10 Sep v12.41 qubit constraint algebra also does not close it — a closed su(2) moment map is not a GR limit.

The 10 Sep simulation shows a constraint algebra can start from quantum relations on a qubit. Gravity’s constraints have not been identified. Do not file Δ_closure = 0 as Friedmann, BBN, CMB, or ADM closure.

Packet contents

MICROSCOPIC_LAW.md — collapse/update candidate: branch superposition, pre-collapse propagation, gravity-induced pruning, innovation amplitude.
OPERATOR_THEOREM.md — admissible operator space; conditions under which Ψ(G_t, R_t) = χ G_t + (1−χ) R_t would be forced at leading order.
CHI_FIXED_POINT.md — χ as a derived quantity instead of a phenomenological one.
CONTINUUM_LIMIT.md — discrete action, coarse-graining, emergent metric, GR-at-leading-order candidate.
COSMOLOGY_BACKGROUND.md — FLRW reduction, modified Friedmann, BBN/CMB consistency.
COSMOLOGY_PERTURBATIONS.md — Newtonian-gauge scalars, growth, lensing, slip.
FAILURE_MODES.md — explicit public ways the package can fail.

No GR recovery, no closed cosmology, no derived χ. Incomplete sections are theorem candidates, proof sketches, derivation targets, or failure points.

The review that forced the packet

The same night, Aaron posted two independent reviews of the RCLC / GEM Bridge program: Grok’s (the in-thread reviewer of the Challenge) and OpenAI’s. Both named the same bottleneck — operator derivation, GR limit, FLRW/BBN/CMB pipeline — and both are why Package 17 is a derivation program rather than another benchmark drop. Neither is a certificate that the derivation succeeded.

The principal unresolved issue is the same one identified in the review you shared: the full Bridge operator and lattice cosmology remain short of a bottom-up derivation from fundamental physics. … Until those pieces are supplied, the framework should be described as a strong conditional prototype with expanding empirical support, not as a complete replacement cosmology.

The posted review upgrades the standard: the bottleneck is foundational closure, not basic seriousness. Package 17 is the public response to that bottleneck. It has not closed it.

The week after: inverted heat-kernel / ADM

7–9 May the GR-bridge work inverted. Stop discretizing Einstein–Hilbert. Recover curvature-like action from retained heat-kernel response. Frozen dx²/long operator; heldout spatial-R 25.15% → 16.55%; next object δρ = A·q; A-channel frozen strict-safe on a synthetic benchmark. Those updates were @grok replies with no Tmp/TOE folder, so the GitHub-first compile missed them. They live on the May 2026 ladder. Full ADM action is still open. This packet did not close because of them.

Heat-kernel week localized the ADM residual. It did not derive Einstein’s equations or close Package 17.
